claims.text: Up to stage-2 DonHangDbContext mapped a Payment class (DbSet<Payment>); at stage-3 it maps no Payment entity, and DonHang.Api neither reads nor writes payment rows. The old payments table stays in donhang, unread.

In docker-compose.yml at stage-3 only the payments service gets Gateway__BaseAddress and Gateway__ApiKey (lines 370-371); the api service has no Gateway setting; fake-gateway also reads Gateway__ApiKey (line 412) to check calls.

Line 367 is the payments connection string: host db, database donhang_payments, user donhang. The api service (line 158) uses the same host db and user donhang with database donhang; only payments and payments-migrate name donhang_payments.

refund-design.md v2 'Vì sao tách': key and money rows are the most sensitive data; in v1 every DonHang.Api copy held the key and could read/write payments; after the split the key is in one service's config, payments in donhang_payments, service deployed/given access/audited alone.
A refund changes data owned by three services: the refund row in Payments (donhang_payments.payments), the order's status in DonHang.Api (donhang.orders) and the customer's email in Notifications.

DonHang.Api saves order.refund-requested in outbox_messages; the relay publishes to donhang.orders; payments.refund-requests (bound with order.refund-requested) feeds RefundRequestedConsumer, inbox + ack after save. Answers go to donhang.payments and reach DonHang.Api via orders.payment-events.

Program.cs lines 20-22 register PaymentsDbContext with UseNpgsql on ConnectionStrings:Default; 27-28 read section Gateway and call AddGatewayRefundClient; 34-36 call AddRabbitMq and AddOutboxRelay<PaymentsDbContext>(exchange: donhang.payments); 37 adds RefundRequestedConsumer.
PaymentsDbContext maps three tables: payments, outbox_messages and inbox_messages.
AddRabbitMq and AddOutboxRelay are defined in the shared project DonHang.Messaging; DonHang.Api calls the same two with exchange donhang.orders.
POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/refund saves the order change and an order.refund-requested outbox row in one transaction and answers 202 Accepted without waiting for Payments.
The refund design rejected calling the gateway inside the customer's request because YC-7 requires accepting a refund request even while the gateway fails.

The Order class decides which status changes are allowed (e.g. Cancel() refuses paid/refunding orders, Ship() refuses refunding ones); a row written to orders from outside DonHang.Api would bypass those rules.

claims.text: Opinion: a waiting HTTP call to Payments adds its downtime to refund failures; with the key out of the many API copies, fewer places can leak it; when one RabbitMQ already serves all services, a second broker adds a server to run, back up and watch, for nothing Payments needs.
claims.source_hint: reasoning from refund-design.md YC-7; design.l3.when-to-extract-a-service (costs of more infrastructure)

claims.text: scripts/backend/rabbitmq-topology.sh prints, under '== bindings on donhang.orders and donhang.payments': donhang.orders --[order.*]--> notifications.order-events, donhang.orders --[order.refund-requested]--> payments.refund-requests, donhang.payments --[payment.*]--> orders.payment-events.
GatewayRefundClient turns the gateway's answers into Đơn Hàng's own RefundOutcome (Refunded, Refused, TryAgainLater), acting as the anti-corruption layer toward the gateway.
At stage-3 DonHang.Api contains no gateway client and no Gateway settings; the only code that calls the payment gateway is GatewayRefundClient in DonHang.Payments.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: grep -ri gateway DonHang.Api (comments only); docker-compose.yml api service 149-198; DonHang.Payments/GatewayRefundClient.cs

claims.text: One PostgreSQL server (cluster) holds several databases isolated from each other; a client connection reaches only the database it names when connecting.
DonHang.Payments/RabbitMqTopology.cs declares exchange donhang.payments, queue payments.refund-requests, and a dead-letter exchange payments.dead-letter with queue payments.refund-requests.dead.
In a topic exchange binding pattern, * matches exactly one dot-separated word, so order.* matches order.refund-requested and notifications.order-events also receives refund requests.
claims.source_hint: RabbitMQ docs, Exchanges > Topic exchange; DonHang.Notifications/OrderEventsConsumer.cs SubjectFor (order.refund-requested)
